# Written by the Gentoo installer: packages that need a lot of memory per compile job.

llvm-core/clang installer-memory
net-libs/webkit-gtk installer-memory
/etc/sysctl.d/80-installer-tuning.conf

# System tuning, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings. Delete this file to go back to the kernel's values.
# A leading "-" lets a kernel without the setting skip it (systemd-sysctl and procps sysctl both read it so).
# Keep more of the directory and file-name cache in memory.
vm.vfs_cache_pressure = 50
# Write changed data to disk early and in smaller amounts, so a large copy does not stall the desktop.
vm.dirty_bytes = 268435456
vm.dirty_background_bytes = 67108864
vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs = 1500
# A longer queue for received network packets.
-net.core.netdev_max_backlog = 4096
# The NMI watchdog costs CPU time and power, and a desktop or laptop does not need it.
-kernel.nmi_watchdog = 0
# zram swaps into compressed memory, which is fast: swap rather than drop the file cache, one page at a time.
vm.swappiness = 150
vm.page-cluster = 0
/etc/udev/rules.d/60-installer-ioschedulers.rules

# I/O schedulers by disk type, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings. Delete this file to use the kernel's choice.
# Hard disks: BFQ keeps the desktop responsive while the disk is busy.
ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="block", KERNEL=="sd[a-z]*", ATTR{queue/rotational}=="1", ATTR{queue/scheduler}="bfq"
# SATA SSDs, SD and eMMC cards: mq-deadline.
ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="block", KERNEL=="sd[a-z]*|mmcblk[0-9]*", ATTR{queue/rotational}=="0", ATTR{queue/scheduler}="mq-deadline"
# NVMe SSDs: Kyber, which keeps reads quick while much is written.
ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="block", KERNEL=="nvme[0-9]*n[0-9]*", ATTR{queue/rotational}=="0", ATTR{queue/scheduler}="kyber"
/etc/tmpfiles.d/installer-thp.conf

# Transparent huge pages, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings. Delete this file to use the kernel's values.
# A program that asks for huge pages gets them without waiting for memory to be compacted.
w! /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag - - - - defer+madvise
# Split a huge page again when most of it (80 percent) is unused, so that memory is not wasted.
w! /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/khugepaged/max_ptes_none - - - - 409
/etc/udev/rules.d/80-installer-audio-power.rules

# Audio power saving only on battery, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings: on the charger it makes some laptops crackle.

ACTION=="add|change", SUBSYSTEM=="power_supply", ENV{POWER_SUPPLY_TYPE}=="Mains", RUN+="/usr/local/libexec/installer-audio-power"
/usr/local/libexec/installer-audio-power

#!/bin/sh
# Audio power saving only on battery, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings.
# udev runs this when the sound card appears and when the charger is plugged in or out (/etc/udev/rules.d/80-installer-audio-power.rules).
param=/sys/module/snd_hda_intel/parameters/power_save
[ -w "$param" ] || exit 0
mains=0
online=0
for supply in /sys/class/power_supply/*; do
	[ "$(cat "$supply/type" 2>/dev/null)" = Mains ] || continue
	mains=1
	[ "$(cat "$supply/online" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] && online=1
done
if [ "$mains" = 1 ] && [ "$online" = 0 ]; then
	echo 1 > "$param"
else
	echo 0 > "$param"
fi
exit 0
/etc/modprobe.d/installer-watchdog.conf

# Watchdog timers, written by the Gentoo installer, values from CachyOS-Settings: a desktop or laptop does not use them, and without them it starts and stops a little faster.
# Delete this file to load them again.
blacklist iTCO_wdt
blacklist sp5100_tco
blacklist wdat_wdt
notes: With 3.8 GiB of memory (and the swap), the packages that need about 4 GiB per compile job (pyside, qtwebengine, llvm, clang, webkit-gtk) get 1 compile job when they are built from source.
post_steps: if getent group pipewire >/dev/null; then usermod -aG pipewire "$1"; fi; exit 0

first_steps: If the screen stays black after an update, choose the boot menu entry that says safe graphics; it starts without the NVIDIA driver.
The NVIDIA modules are rebuilt by emerge after every kernel update (USE=dist-kernel). If an update reports that the build failed, run: emerge --ask @module-rebuild
notes: Portable install: both Intel and AMD microcode are installed.
NVIDIA proprietary driver 595 (current, open kernel modules); if it fails to build, the open nouveau driver stays in use.
The NVIDIA driver is not on the binary host: it is downloaded from download.nvidia.com and compiled on this PC, which adds several minutes and needs internet access to that address.
With 3.8 GiB of memory (and the swap), the packages that need about 4 GiB per compile job (pyside, qtwebengine, llvm, clang, webkit-gtk) get 1 compile job when they are built from source.
post_steps: if [ ! -f /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf ] && [ -d "/home/$1" ]; then printf "%s\n" "$2" >> "/home/$1/first-steps.txt"; chown "$1:$(id -gn "$1")" "/home/$1/first-steps.txt"; fi; exit 0

The NVIDIA driver could not be installed during the installation, so this PC runs on the open nouveau driver. To try again once the network works: emerge --ask x11-drivers/nvidia-drivers && dracut --force --regenerate-all (the driver is downloaded from download.nvidia.com and compiled on this PC).
if getent group pipewire >/dev/null; then usermod -aG pipewire "$1"; fi; exit 0

set -- /var/db/pkg/app-misc/hwmonux-*; if [ -f /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf ] && [ -d "$1" ]; then echo 'app-misc/hwmonux nvidia' > /etc/portage/package.use/installer-hwmonux-nvidia && emerge --oneshot app-misc/hwmonux || { rm -f /etc/portage/package.use/installer-hwmonux-nvidia; echo 'HWMonux NVIDIA sensors skipped'; }; fi; exit 0

Firmware: Linux firmware (AMD graphics, Ethernet adapter)
Memory: compressed RAM swap (zram), 1953 MiB
Memory: large programs that have to be compiled (Qt, LLVM, PySide) are built with one compile job, to stay within the memory of this PC
Tuning: /etc/sysctl.d/80-installer-tuning.conf, memory and disk-write settings and swap settings for zram (applied by systemd-sysctl)
Tuning: zswap.enabled=0 on the kernel command line, because zram does the swapping
Tuning: /etc/udev/rules.d/60-installer-ioschedulers.rules, BFQ for hard disks, mq-deadline for SATA SSDs and cards, Kyber for NVMe (udev)
Tuning: /etc/tmpfiles.d/installer-thp.conf, huge pages for programs that ask for them (applied by systemd-tmpfiles-setup)
Tuning: /etc/udev/rules.d/80-installer-audio-power.rules, audio power saving only on battery, which stops crackling (udev)
Tuning: /etc/modprobe.d/installer-watchdog.conf, the unused watchdog timers are not loaded
